clue.text: Allergen so upset cell components

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or thrown into disorder, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's allergy appears to be playing havoc with their cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' tells you to rearrange the ten letters of ALLERGEN and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Organelles are the specialised structures, such as mitochondria, found inside a living cell.

clue.text: Cockney bands offering a word of apology

indicators.note: Cockney speech traditionally drops the H at the start of a word, so the opening H goes

explanation.surface: A London band says sorry for its performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, famous for dropping the H: 'hoops' said by a Cockney comes out as 'oops'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone says on making a small mistake, a quick apology.

clue.text: Monster to smile if female is caught

parts.note: to grin is to smile broadly
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'is caught' is the container signal: the smile word holds both IF and the F for female.
explanation.definitionFit: A griffin is a mythical beast with an eagle's head and wings on a lion's body.

clue.text: Ron had to divert around rugged track blocked at end

parts.note: rugged ground is rough

explanation.surface: Ron must take a detour around a bumpy track that comes to a dead end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divert' rearranges RON HAD TO into NOTHROAD, and 'around' wraps those letters round ROUGH: NOTH-ROUGH-ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign saying this marks a lane that is closed off at its far end, a cul-de-sac.

clue.text: Writing something for the minutes

definitions.meaning: ordinary handwriting with the words spelled out in full, as opposed to shorthand or typing
on a clock face, the longer pointer shows the minutes

explanation.definitionFit: Script written out fully by pen is one sense; the longer pointer on a clock dial, which marks minutes, is the other.

clue.text: Provide English with something to laugh at

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark, made to be laughed at

explanation.surface: Someone supplies an Englishman with a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish or supply them with what they need.

clue.text: With Mrs Mopp glamour is in short supply

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the glamour word loses its last letter

parts.note: charm is attractiveness or allure, a synonym for glamour

explanation.surface: The cleaning lady is hardly a glamorous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Mopp was the charlady in the 1940s BBC radio comedy ITMA, and a 'char' is a British word for a cleaning woman; CHARM loses its final M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Mopp, the office cleaner of a famous radio comedy, has become a byword for a cleaning lady.

clue.text: Uncomfortable situation provided by 11?

definitions.meaning: a position where one is under pressure or has to answer awkward questions
the electric chair of 11 down is slang-named for the seat that gets hot

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a position of pressure or scrutiny, and in American slang it also names the execution chair.

clue.text: Ruddy optimistic!

definitions.meaning: having a reddish colour, like a pink flower
seeing things as better than they are, as through coloured glasses

explanation.definitionFit: Literally tinged with a pinkish red, and figuratively hopeful to the point of naivety, as in seeing the world through coloured spectacles.

clue.text: Tip for cricketer in the field

definitions.meaning: the sharp end of something, like a pencil
a fielding position on the off side, square of the batsman

explanation.definitionFit: The sharp end of a needle is one sense; a cricket fielder stationed near the batsman on the off side is the other.

clue.text: Revolts disturbing USA senate

indicators.note: disturbing means throwing into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Americans are upset by something going on in the US Senate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' rearranges USA and SENATE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sickens or disgusts someone revolts them, the verb sense.

clue.text: A shocking thing for some doomed to die

definitions.text: A shocking thing for some doomed to die

parts.words: A shocking thing for some doomed to die
parts.note: shocking is read literally, as giving an electric shock, to condemned prisoners in the American execution system

clue.text: What the Christmas wrapping paper may be, temporarily

definitions.text: What the Christmas wrapping paper may be
definitions.meaning: gift paper is intended to go round a gift
for now, for the time being

explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping paper exists to cover a gift; the same phrase is an idiom meaning for the time being.

clue.text: Huntsman's turning in with drink and not getting up in the morning?

definitions.text: not getting up in the morning?

parts.note: John Peel was the huntsman of the song D'ye Ken John Peel, so Peel's

gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.definitionFit: Lying in bed past the usual hour of rising is what staying under the covers late means.

clue.text: Pasta and fish — universal home fare ultimately?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of fare

explanation.surface: Pasta with fish, the kind of home cooking everyone ends up eating.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguine is a type of flat, narrow noodle from Italy.

clue.text: Disclose name for a new York island

parts.note: to state is to declare or reveal

explanation.surface: Reveal what a newly founded island in York is called.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital N of 'new' has been moved to 'York', so 'new York' reads as a fresh island off the English city when it means one in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Staten Island is one of the five boroughs of New York City.

clue.text: Reasoning a break can be held together by glue

indicators.note: the break is held together with the glue sitting inside it

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
gum is an adhesive

explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a line of reasoning set out to support a claim.

clue.text: It's crude? It gets your attention initially

thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A coarse joke is bound to grab your attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It gets ... initially' says that THY (your) gets EAR (attention) at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse, frank and down-to-earth.

clue.text: What takes time after day with wet weather?

an age is a long period of time

oil is a thick, slow-flowing liquid

clue.text: Big and impressive but badly organised
